scope: 32 units missing from the original 3117-entry index, all defined in linked W3C publications predating 2026-10-29. No browser version claims are added.

units.name: rex
units.meaning: A root-font-relative length based on the x-height of the root element’s first available font. Font metrics and writing mode affect the result according to the unit’s definition.
units.where: Use it where a length is accepted when sizing should follow root font metrics rather than a nested component’s font.

units.name: rcap
units.meaning: A root-font-relative length based on the cap-height of the root element’s first available font. Font metrics and writing mode affect the result according to the unit’s definition.
units.where: Use it where a length is accepted when sizing should follow root font metrics rather than a nested component’s font.

units.name: rch
units.meaning: A root-font-relative length based on the advance measure of the “0” glyph of the root element’s first available font. Font metrics and writing mode affect the result according to the unit’s definition.
units.where: Use it where a length is accepted when sizing should follow root font metrics rather than a nested component’s font.

units.name: ric
units.meaning: A root-font-relative length based on the advance measure of the ideographic water glyph (水) of the root element’s first available font. Font metrics and writing mode affect the result according to the unit’s definition.
units.where: Use it where a length is accepted when sizing should follow root font metrics rather than a nested component’s font.

units.name: lh
units.meaning: A length based on the computed line height of the element, with normal resolved using font metrics. Using it does not itself limit a box to a particular number of actual lines.
units.where: Use it for spacing that should follow the text’s line-height rhythm. Special parent/initial-metric rules avoid circular definitions in font and line-height declarations.

units.name: rlh
units.meaning: A length based on the computed line height of the root element, with normal resolved using font metrics. Using it does not itself limit a box to a particular number of actual lines.
units.where: Use it for spacing that should follow the text’s line-height rhythm. Special parent/initial-metric rules avoid circular definitions in font and line-height declarations.

units.name: vi
units.meaning: One vi is one percent of the inline size of the large viewport. The large viewport assumes retractable browser interfaces are retracted, so visible browser controls can cover content.
units.where: Use it where a length is accepted. Choose small, large or dynamic viewport behavior deliberately, and test browser controls and writing modes.

units.name: cqw
units.meaning: One cqw is one percent of the relevant query container’s width. When no eligible query container exists for an axis, the small viewport size supplies the fallback for that axis.
units.where: Use it on descendants of a size-query container to make a component respond to its container rather than directly to the viewport. Eligibility is determined separately for each axis.
